name: n08-ndots
title: ndots and search domain expansion
spec: Left: a pod's resolv.conf in monospace: 'search my-ns.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local dc1.example.com', 'nameserver 10.96.0.10', 'options ndots:5'. Right: a lookup of api.example.com (2 dots, fewer than 5) producing a vertical list of tried names in order: api.example.com.my-ns.svc.cluster.local, then ...svc.cluster.local, then ...cluster.local, then ...dc1.example.com, finally the name itself (orange for the failing wasted ones). Bottom fixes row: 'FQDN with trailing dot', 'dnsConfig.options ndots: 1 or 2', 'NodeLocal DNSCache'.
alt: ndots search expansion in a pod
cap: A name with fewer dots than ndots is tried through every search domain before the real name.

name: n08-5sec
title: The random 5-second delay
spec: Sequence between pod and CoreDNS via node conntrack: pod sends two UDP queries, A and AAAA, from the same source port within microseconds; the AAAA query is lost in conntrack (orange X, race on same-5-tuple UDP flows through NAT); resolver waits 5 s (glibc timeout) then retries and the call stalls. Side fixes in monospace: 'single-request-reopen', 'use-vc', NodeLocal DNSCache, kernel upgrade. Green bar: 'Match the number of seconds to a timer and you will find the layer'.
anchor: ## 11. Case study: "random 5-second delays" in a GPU inference cluster
cap: Two parallel UDP queries can race in conntrack, so one is lost and the resolver waits for its 5 second timeout.
